external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches and can manually trigger a rebuild of main.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry on the internet used during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves dependencies, produces container images, pushes images, calls the deploy controller, and permits manual rebuilds.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Receives release requests and answers store-server queries about the current release.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small back-office server that polls the deploy controller, pulls changed images, and restarts the container.
processes.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 store servers, one at each store.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Till software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

data_stores.name: git server
data_stores.description: Self-hosted git server containing developer branches and the main branch.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: Registry storing finished container images tagged with commit SHA.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores. The registry allows store-server pulls.

data_stores.name: deploy controller release record
data_stores.description: The record identifying which image SHA the estate should be running.
data_stores.source_excerpt: holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on
data_stores.notes: This is the record held by the deploy controller.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: Developer pushes branches to the self-hosted git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: Build runner fetches source from the git server after a merge.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: Build runner reaches out to the public package registry to resolve dependencies.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.
data_flows.data_description: Dependencies downloaded according to the lockfile

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: Build runner pushes the finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.
data_flows.data_description: Finished container image tagged with commit SHA

data_flows.name: make release current
data_flows.description: Build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: Image SHA and shared build token

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer manually triggers a rebuild of main on the build runner.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

data_flows.name: ask current release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller for the current release once a minute.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the release image from the image registry when its running image differs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull; nobody has written down what a store server presents to it.
data_flows.data_description: Container image for the current release

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: Corporate network containing the git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: Separate build environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The estate of approximately 1,200 stores containing the store servers.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.
trust_boundaries.notes: Traffic between the stores and the corporate network goes over the retail WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet reached during dependency resolution.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The source code and branches held by the git server are commercially sensitive build records.
assumptions.basis: The git server holds developer branches and source for the build pipeline.

assumptions.assumption: The container images held by the image registry are commercially sensitive build artifacts.
assumptions.basis: The image registry holds finished container images deployed to the store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The deploy controller release record is commercially sensitive operational data.
assumptions.basis: The record determines which image SHA the estate should run.

assumptions.assumption: The developer branches and source carried to the git server are business-critical operating records.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries source changes used by the build and deployment pipeline.

assumptions.assumption: The source fetched by the build runner is a business-critical build artifact.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries merged source used to produce the deployed container image.

assumptions.assumption: The dependencies downloaded by the build runner are business-critical build inputs.
assumptions.basis: The flow supplies dependencies used to produce deployed container images.

assumptions.assumption: The finished container image is a business-critical deployment artifact.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries the finished image that is deployed to the store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The release request carries a business-critical image SHA.
assumptions.basis: The runner asks the controller to make an image the current estate release.

assumptions.assumption: The manual rebuild request concerns a business-critical build.
assumptions.basis: The request triggers a rebuild of main.

assumptions.assumption: The current release image SHA is business-critical operational data.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries the release selected for the store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The pulled container image is a business-critical deployment artifact.
assumptions.basis: The flow carries the image used to restart the till container.
